verses.1:1: Pronouncement concerning Nineveh, the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
verses.1:2: The Lord is a jealous God, taking vengeance with fury; the Lord takes vengeance on His adversaries, and He Himself removes His enemies.
verses.1:3: The Lord is slow to anger, and great is His strength, and the Lord will not acquit as innocent; His way is in complete destruction and in a tempest, and clouds are the dust of His feet,
verses.1:4: threatening the sea and drying it up, and making all the rivers desolate. Bashan and Carmel diminished, and the blossoms of Lebanon failed.
verses.1:5: The mountains were shaken before Him, and the hills reeled; and the earth recoiled from His presence, the entire world, and all who dwell in it.
verses.1:6: Before His wrath, who will stand firm? And who will withstand in the wrath of His fury? His fury melts dominions, and the rocks were shattered before Him.
verses.1:7: The Lord is good to those who wait for Him in a day of distress, and knows those who revere Him.
verses.1:8: And with an advancing flood He will bring about complete destruction; darkness will pursue those who rise up and His enemies.
verses.1:9: What are you scheming against the Lord? He Himself will bring about complete destruction; He will not take vengeance twice at the same time in distress,
verses.1:10: for down to its foundation it will be laid waste, and like intertwined bindweed it will be devoured, and like stubble full of dryness.
verses.1:11: Out of you will come forth a scheme against the Lord, devising evil, contrary things.
verses.1:12: Thus says the Lord, who rules over many waters: "Even so they will be separated, and the report of you will no longer be heard.
verses.1:13: And now I will shatter his rod from off you, and I will tear the bonds apart."
verses.1:14: And the Lord will give a command concerning you: "No more will be sown from your name; from the house of your god I will utterly destroy the carved images, and I will make cast images your grave." For swift,
verses.2:1: Look, upon the mountains are the feet of one proclaiming good news and announcing peace. Celebrate your festivals, Judah; pay your vows, because they will certainly never again pass through you to decay.
verses.2:2: It has been brought to an end; it has been removed. One breathing into your face has come up, rescuing from distress. Watch the road, take hold of your loins, be exceedingly courageous in strength;
verses.2:3: for the Lord has turned back the insolence of Jacob, just as the insolence of Israel, because, shaking out, they shook them and their vine branches out. They destroyed
verses.2:4: the weapons of their power from among men, mighty men mocking in fire; the reins of their chariots in the day of his preparation, and the horsemen will be thrown into uproar
verses.2:5: in the roads, and the chariots will be thrown into confusion and will become entangled in the broad squares; their appearance is like torches of fire and like lightning flashes darting about.
verses.2:6: And their nobles will remember, and they will flee by day and grow weak in their march, and they will hurry to her walls and prepare their outposts.
verses.2:7: The gates of the cities were opened wide, and the palace collapsed,
verses.2:8: and the foundation was uncovered, and she was going up, and her female servants were being led away like doves moaning in their hearts.
verses.2:9: And Nineveh, like a pool of water are her waters, and they, fleeing, did not stop, and there was no one looking back.
verses.2:10: They plundered the silver, they were plundering the gold, and there was no end to her adornment; they have been weighed down over all her desirable vessels.
verses.2:11: Shaking out and shaking up and upheaval and shattering of heart, and loosening of knees and labor pains upon all loins, and the face of all is like the scorching of a pot.
verses.2:12: Where is the dwelling place of the lions, and the pasture belonging to the cubs? Where did a lion go for a lion's cub to enter there, and there was no one causing terror?
verses.2:13: A lion seized enough for his cubs and strangled for his lions, and he filled his lair with prey and his dwelling place with plunder.
verses.2:14: "Look, I am against you," says the Lord Almighty, "and I will burn up your multitude in smoke, and a sword will devour your lions, and I will utterly destroy your prey from the earth, and your deeds will certainly never be heard again."
verses.3:1: Ah, city of bloodshed, wholly false, full of injustice, prey will not be handled.
verses.3:2: The sound of whips and the sound of the shaking of wheels, and of a pursuing horse and of a jolting chariot,
verses.3:3: and of a horseman going up and of a gleaming sword and of flashing weapons, and of a multitude of wounded and of a heavy fall; and there was no end to her nations, and they will grow weak in their bodies from a multitude of prostitution.
verses.3:4: A beautiful and charming prostitute, mistress of sorceries, who sells nations by her prostitution and peoples by her sorceries.
verses.3:5: "Look, I am against you," says the Lord God Almighty, "and I will uncover your back parts over your face, and I will show nations your shame and kingdoms your dishonor;
verses.3:6: and I will throw abomination upon you according to your impurities, and I will make you an example;
verses.3:7: and it will happen that everyone who sees you will go down from you and will say, 'Wretched Nineveh! Who will groan over her? From where will I seek comfort for her?'"
verses.3:8: Prepare a portion, tune the string, prepare a portion, Ammon, who dwells among rivers; water is around her, whose dominion is the sea, and water is her walls.
verses.3:9: And Ethiopia is her strength, and Egypt, and there is no end to the flight, and Libyans became her helpers.
verses.3:10: And she herself will go into exile as a captive, and they will dash her infants to the ground at the heads of all her streets, and over all her glorious things they will cast lots, and all her nobles will be bound with manacles.
verses.3:11: You too will become drunk and will be overlooked, and you too will seek for yourself a standing place away from enemies.
verses.3:12: All your strongholds are fig trees having watchmen; if they are shaken, they will fall into the mouth of one who eats.
verses.3:13: Look, your people are like women in your midst; to your enemies the gates of your land will certainly be opened; fire will devour your bars.
verses.3:14: Draw siege water for yourself, and strengthen your strongholds; step into the clay and be trampled in straw; grow stronger than brick.
verses.3:15: There fire will devour you, a sword will utterly destroy you, it will devour you like a locust, and you will be weighed down like a young locust.
verses.3:16: You multiplied your commercial dealings more than the stars of heaven; a young locust rushed forward and flew away.
verses.3:17: Your mixed multitude leaped out like a grasshopper, like a locust settled on a fence on a day of frost; the sun rose, and it leaped away, and it did not know its place. Woe to them!
verses.3:18: Your shepherds slumbered, Assyrian king; he put your rulers to sleep; your people departed to the mountains, and there was no one receiving them.
verses.3:19: There is no healing for your fracture, your wound has become inflamed; all who hear the news about you will clap their hands over you; for upon whom has your wickedness not come continually?

notes.1:3: Greek ἀθῷον οὐκ ἀθῳώσει (literally "as innocent He will not acquit") reproduces the Hebrew emphatic construction ("will by no means acquit"). Likewise, "in complete destruction" translates Greek συντελείᾳ, connecting Hebrew suphah ("whirlwind") with the root suph ("come to an end").
notes.1:6: The Greek reads "melts dominions" (τήκει ἀρχάς), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "is poured out like fire."
notes.1:7: The Greek reads "to those who wait for Him" and "those who revere Him," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "a stronghold" and "those who take refuge in Him."
notes.1:12: The Greek "who rules over many waters" (κατάρχων ὑδάτων πολλῶν) differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("Though they are at full strength and likewise many") through a different division and vocalization of the Hebrew consonants.
notes.1:14: The closing words "For swift" (ὅτι ταχεῖς) render Hebrew qallota ("you are vile") as a plural adjective linked syntactically to "the feet" at the opening of 2:1. The Greek punctuation also places "cast images" as the object of "I will make... your grave."
notes.2:1: The Greek "to decay" (εἰς παλαίωσιν) renders Hebrew beliyya'al ("worthlessness / the wicked one") by connecting it with the root meaning "to grow old, wear out."
notes.2:2: The Greek reads "One breathing into your face... rescuing from distress," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "A scatterer has come up against you; guard the rampart."
notes.2:4: The verb "They destroyed" at the end of 2:3 governs the accusative phrases opening 2:4 in the Greek syntax. The Greek "from among men" and "mocking" reflect different readings of the Hebrew terms translated "dyed red" and "in scarlet."
notes.2:7: The Greek reads "gates of the cities" (πόλεων) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "gates of the rivers," likely reflecting an early inner-Greek transcriptional variant for ποταμῶν.
notes.2:14: The Greek reads "your multitude" (πλῆθός σου) and "your deeds" (τὰ ἔργα σου), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "her chariots" and "the voice of your messengers."
notes.3:1: The Greek "prey will not be handled" (οὐ ψηλαφηθήσεται θήρα) renders Hebrew yamish ("depart") by linking it with the root mashash ("to feel, grope").
notes.3:3: The Greek reads "to her nations" (τοῖς ἔθνεσιν αὐτῆς) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "to the corpses," and places "from a multitude of prostitution" at the close of 3:3 rather than at the start of 3:4.
notes.3:8: The Greek retains the proper name "Ammon" (Ἀμμών) and renders the opening Hebrew question ("Are you better than No-Amon [Thebes]?") as imperatives ("Prepare a portion, tune the string, prepare a portion, Ammon").
notes.3:12: The Greek reads "fig trees having watchmen" (συκαῖ σκοποὺς ἔχουσαι), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "fig trees with first-ripe figs."
notes.3:17: The Greek reads "Your mixed multitude," uses the active verb "it did not know its place," and ends with "Woe to them!" (οὐαὶ αὐτοῖς), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text asks "Where are they?"
